checks.detail: Python 3.9 (`python3`) is below the effective floor 3.12, which comes from /home/dev/zephyrproject/zephyr/cmake/modules/python.cmake. The build does not fail here -- it fails later, inside Zephyr's own CMake configure, with an error that names Zephyr rather than your Python.

checks.name: pythonFloor
checks.detail: alp-sdk's metadata/bootstrap.json declares pythonMinVersion 3.10, but the build's effective floor is 3.12 (from /home/dev/zephyrproject/zephyr/cmake/modules/python.cmake). Both `tan doctor` and `tan bootstrap` enforce the higher, effective floor, so a host this manifest would have accepted is refused up front rather than failing later at Zephyr's CMake configure.
checks.fix: Known, Zephyr-scoped skew (alp-sdk#1078) -- raising `prerequisites.pythonMinVersion` to 3.12 was tried and reverted, because that key also gates Yocto-only and metadata-only projects, which do not need it. Building for Zephyr on a host below 3.12 needs a newer interpreter -- see the `hostPython` check above.

checks.name: west
checks.detail: `west` is not on bare PATH, but resolves through the workspace venv: /home/dev/zephyrproject/.venv/bin/west -- the same binary `westResolved` above reports, and the one a real build actually spawns. This is the default state right after `tan bootstrap`, which deliberately does not put `west` on PATH; activating the venv (its `bin`/`Scripts` directory holds the `west` launcher) would additionally put it on bare PATH, for tools that spawn it directly rather than through tan.

checks.name: devicetreeLint
checks.detail: no `dtc` in CMake's reach (neither a Zephyr SDK `hosttools/` copy nor one on PATH), so Zephyr's devicetree lint pass (`-E unit_address_vs_reg` / `-Wunique_unit_address_if_enabled`) is SKIPPED -- `dts.cmake` guards it with `if(DTC)` and treats dtc as optional. Builds succeed and produce a real `zephyr.elf`; only those diagnostics are absent. This is the expected state after `tan bootstrap`, which acquires the Zephyr SDK with `--no-hosttools` (tan-cli#1178) and so installs no dtc. Install a system dtc 1.4.6 or newer if you want the lint back.

checks.name: setools
checks.detail: AEN MRAM flashing (Flow D `alif_mram_jlink`, the planner default, and Flow A `west flash`) cannot sign an ATOC: $SETOOLS_DIR is unset (the Alif Security Toolkit is license-gated and NOT redistributed by alp-sdk). Flow A (`west flash`, alif_flash) is Linux-only in this tree -- run it from WSL2/Linux.
checks.fix: Download the Alif Security Toolkit (`app-release-exec-linux-SE_FW_x.y.z`) from the Alif developer portal -- it is license-gated and alp-sdk does not redistribute it -- then `export SETOOLS_DIR=<...>/app-release-exec-linux`. Flow A (`west flash`) additionally needs `export SE_UART=/dev/ttyUSB0` (your SE-UART device); Flow D does not. See docs/aen-bench-bringup.md. Doctor reads $SETOOLS_DIR and the built manifest's flash_args.setools_dir; a --setools-dir flag given to `tan flash` is not visible to it.

checks.name: jlink
checks.detail: J-Link tools found at /usr/bin/JLink but their version could not be read, so the Flow D MRAM loader could not be confirmed. Flow D needs the `AE822FA0E5597LS0_M55_HE` part-number device profile (NOT the generic `Cortex-M55`, which has no MRAM loader) and a J-Link DLL V9.46+. Device profile resolved from: /home/dev/alp-sdk/metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e8.json.
checks.fix: Run `JLinkExe` by hand (it prints the banner unprompted, then type `exit`) and confirm it reports V9.46 or newer.

Download the Alif Security Toolkit (`app-release-exec-linux-SE_FW_x.y.z`) from the Alif developer portal -- it is license-gated and alp-sdk does not redistribute it -- then `export SETOOLS_DIR=<...>/app-release-exec-linux`. Flow A (`west flash`) additionally needs `export SE_UART=/dev/ttyUSB0` (your SE-UART device); Flow D does not. See docs/aen-bench-bringup.md. Doctor reads $SETOOLS_DIR and the built manifest's flash_args.setools_dir; a --setools-dir flag given to `tan flash` is not visible to it.
